rules.rationale: Prevents ambiguous payment finality and downstream ticket issuance drift.
rules.text: If money_state == paid_confirmed then verified_payment_attempt_id and paid_confirmed_at_utc MUST be non-null and emitted exclusively by verify_payment_reference; no other operation may produce paid_confirmed.

rules.rationale: Prevents 'paid_confirmed' without immutable proof pointer; blocks spoofing and supports auditability.
rules.text: When verify_payment_reference returns money_state == "paid_confirmed", evidence_digest_sha256 MUST be non-null and MUST identify immutable payment proof bytes stored by the platform (e.g., provider receipt JSON / PSP signed artifact). The digest MUST be stable for the same provider + provider_reference_id.

rules.details: money_state MUST be one of: paid_confirmed, pending, failed, awaiting_manual_verification, payment_plan_active, on_hold. Only paid_confirmed MAY be treated as sufficient to issue tickets (TKT-1) or admit (SCAN-1). awaiting_manual_verification is used for manual EFT/cash flows pending operator attestation. payment_plan_active is used when installments are accepted but the order MUST NOT be finalized as paid until the plan completes. on_hold is used when a provider authorization/chargeback/compliance hold prevents settlement.
rules.rule: PAY-1 money_state vocabulary is authoritative across the suite.

rules.details: payment_reference_c14n MUST be computed as: 'payref_c14n/v1:' + provider + ':' + sha256_hex(provider_reference_id). payment_reference_c14n MUST NOT include the raw provider_reference_id. Systems MAY log payment_reference_c14n and MUST NOT log raw provider_reference_id unless required for support with explicit access controls.
rules.rule: PAY-1 defines payment_reference_c14n for safe correlation in logs and signatures.

rules.rationale: Prevents the GC-001 “late capture after hold expiry” race by enforcing orchestration call-order and fail-closed behavior.
rules.text: The application MUST arm ORD-1 payment grace (Order.payment_grace_expires_at_utc set and in the future) AND extend any SEAT holds before calling PAY-1.initialize_payment or PAY-1.confirm_or_capture. PAY-1 implementations MUST treat missing/invalid tenant or payment_intent context as fail-closed (ERR_FORBIDDEN or ERR_BAD_REQUEST) and MUST NOT proceed with provider initialization/capture.

rules.rationale: Ensures payment finality timestamps are authoritative and supports deterministic late-capture windows (SD-043).
rules.text: When money_state == paid_confirmed, paid_confirmed_at_utc MUST represent a provider-confirmed timestamp (provider event creation/processing time or provider receipt time that is authoritative). It MUST NOT be derived from local ingest time. If provider-confirmed time is unavailable, money_state MUST NOT be paid_confirmed (use pending or awaiting_manual_verification).

rules.rationale: Stops “phantom payment time” drift which otherwise breaks grace/hold expiry comparisons.
rules.text: parse_event.occurred_at MUST be sourced from provider payload metadata when available. If a provider does not emit a timestamp, occurred_at MUST be derived from an authoritative provider processing/receipt time (not local ingest time) or the event MUST be rejected as unverifiable (ERR_BAD_REQUEST).

PaymentIntent MUST include a non-null `order_id` (uuid_v7) and this `order_id` MUST be immutable after creation. Payment authorization/capture MUST NOT proceed unless the referenced ORD-1 order exists and is `pending`.

verify_payment_reference MUST require `expected_order_id` and MUST return `order_id` and `payment_intent_id`. If the provider reference resolves to a different order_id than expected, the operation MUST error (swap/replay defense).

For any transition to `paid_confirmed`, PAY-1 MUST persist and expose `provider_confirmed_at_utc` from the provider/gateway as the authoritative time. Application server time MUST NOT be used as provider-confirmed time.

If provider confirms payment for an order already terminal (`canceled` or `expired`), PAY-1 MUST emit OBS-1 `audit_recovery` with {org_id, order_id, payment_intent_id, provider_reference_id, provider_confirmed_at_utc} and MUST flag funds for deterministic disposition (refund or unallocated credit journaling).

sections.text: All public error envelopes MUST emit ERR-1 primary codes with underscores (e.g., ERR_BAD_REQUEST, ERR_CONFLICT, ERR_FORBIDDEN). Implementations MUST NOT emit underscore-less aliases (e.g., ERRBADREQUEST).

summary: Defines the hard boundary between the core payments domain and external PSP providers (Stripe/Paystack/PayFast/etc), including idempotency, webhook safety, tenancy isolation, and ledger separation.

summary_detail.one_liner: Defines the hard boundary between the core payments domain and external PSP providers (Stripe/Paystack/PayFast/etc), including idempotency, webhook safety, tenancy isolation, and ledger separation.
summary_detail.problem: Payments integrations fail in the denial paths: duplicate webhooks, replay attacks, cross-tenant routing mistakes, and accidental ledger coupling. Without a strict adapter contract, every PSP integration invents its own semantics.
summary_detail.solution: A single PSP adapter interface with mandatory security, idempotency, and tenancy invariants; all PSP input is normalized into core domain resources/events; the adapter may never mutate core tables directly nor decide ledger postings.

anti_patterns: Performing heavy work synchronously inside webhook handler before persisting to durable storage/queue.
Using 'ticket lookup' or 'transaction lookup' endpoints that allow enumeration of valid IDs.
Routing tenant by untrusted URL params without signature-bound metadata.
Double-key dedupe (provider + provider_event_id) is forbidden in multi-account environments; dedupe_key MUST include provider_account_ref.
